subject: mathematics
title: Place in Line
objective: Read and use ordinal numbers up to the 100th to show position.
introduction: Runners line up for Milo’s relay. Can you name who is 1st, 2nd, 10th, and 100th?

items.prompt: Which shows the position of the first child in line?
items.explanation: 1st names the first position in line. 8th names the eighth position, and counts like '8 children' or '1' do not name a place in line.

items.prompt: Which shows the position right after first?
items.explanation: 2nd (second) comes right after 1st (first). 3rd comes after 2nd, and a plain count of 2 is not a position.

items.prompt: Which shows the position of the tenth child in line?
items.explanation: 10th names the tenth position in line. '10 children' or '10' alone is a count, not a position.

items.prompt: Which shows the position of the 100th runner in a race?
items.explanation: 100th names the one-hundredth position in the race. 99th is a different position, and '100' is a count, not a place.
1st is an ordinal number because it names a position. The other choices give counts, not places in a line.
